themes_detail.label: Rodent Infestation Spike
themes_detail.summary: Rodent complaints in Central Harlem surged to 39 this week, more than double the 8-week average of 18.4 complaints per week, suggesting a possible infestation outbreak or seasonal acceleration that warrants immediate investigation into underlying sanitation and housing conditions.
evidence: 39 rodent complaints THIS WEEK vs. 18.4-complaint weekly average over prior 8 weeks (112% spike, z-score: 3.6)
Spike coincides with unsanitary condition complaints remaining at 1,225 over 90 days, suggesting poor sanitation infrastructure
Aligns with community board's recurring budget request for facility upgrades and maintenance equipment, indicating chronic infrastructure neglect
reporting_angles: Interview residents in buildings with multiple 311 complaints to document health impacts and housing conditions
Investigate whether Department of Health rat mitigation efforts are reaching Central Harlem or if gaps exist in baiting/inspection coverage
Report on why community board's infrastructure upgrade requests remain unfunded year after year despite persistent pest complaints

themes_detail.label: Construction Surge Without Oversight
themes_detail.summary: General construction and plumbing complaints tripled this past week to 24 (vs. 9.1-week average), coinciding with 485 building permits filed in the last 90 days (411 alterations), raising questions about whether construction activity is outpacing city inspection capacity and resident complaint resolution.
evidence: 24 construction/plumbing complaints last week vs. 9.1-complaint weekly baseline (163% spike, z-score: 5.48, highest statistical severity)
485 total building permits filed in last 90 days, with 411 alteration permits indicating heavy renovation activity across district
Concurrent 62% spike in appliance complaints (28 vs. 17.2 avg) suggests construction may be damaging building systems
reporting_angles: Map construction permit clusters against 311 complaint hotspots to identify neighborhoods experiencing worst oversight gaps
Interview DOB about inspection staffing levels for Central Harlem and whether complaint response times are meeting SLAs
Investigate whether ULURP projects (254 West 124th, One45, Frederick Douglass Blvd) are generating ancillary construction complaints in surrounding blocks

themes_detail.label: Dead animal & sanitation complaints
themes_detail.summary: Dead animal complaints spiked 500% this past week (3 vs. 0.5-complaint baseline), and combined with ongoing unsanitary condition complaints (1,225 over 90 days), this signals a possible public health and waste management failure in street cleaning or animal disposal services.
evidence: 3 dead animal complaints last week vs. 0.5-complaint weekly average (500% spike, z-score: 5.0)
Unsanitary condition complaints total 1,225 over 90 days, indicating chronic street and sanitation management issues
Dirty condition complaints add another 493 complaints, compounding perception of neighborhood neglect
reporting_angles: Obtain DSNY complaint and response logs to determine if dead animal removal SLA is being met and why lag times exist
Document specific streets and blocks with repeated unsanitary and dirty condition complaints to map sanitation coverage gaps
Interview residents about health concerns and disease vectors, particularly in relation to rodent spike occurring simultaneously

themes_detail.label: Illegal Tree Damage & Environmental Violations
themes_detail.summary: Illegal tree damage complaints tripled last week (3 vs. 1.0-complaint average), concurrent with air quality complaints doubling (6 vs. 2.0 average), suggesting possible construction-related environmental violations or inadequate tree protection enforcement during the active permit season.
evidence: 3 illegal tree damage complaints last week vs. 1.0-complaint weekly average (200% spike, z-score: 4.0)
6 air quality complaints last week vs. 2.0-complaint weekly average (200% spike, z-score: 3.27)
Spike timing aligns with peak construction season (485 permits filed in 90 days) and contractor activity
reporting_angles: Obtain Parks Department enforcement data on illegal tree removal/damage citations and penalties in Central Harlem over past month
Identify whether air quality complaints cluster around active construction sites or relate to dust/debris from demolition permits
Interview environmental advocates about whether tree canopy loss in Central Harlem is being tracked and whether mitigation is required in ULURP approvals

themes_detail.label: Residential Waste Disposal Strain
themes_detail.summary: Residential disposal complaints spiked 220% two weeks ago (10 vs. 3.1-complaint average) and remain elevated, suggesting garbage collection or waste management service gaps that may be compounding the broader sanitation problem evident across multiple 311 complaint categories.
evidence: 10 residential disposal complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 3.1-complaint weekly average (220% spike, z-score: 3.75)
Aligns with ongoing unsanitary condition complaints (1,225 over 90 days), suggesting systemic waste management failure
Precedes or parallels dead animal and sanitation spikes, indicating connected service degradation
reporting_angles: Interview DSNY about collection schedule changes or staffing shortfalls affecting Central Harlem in past 3 weeks
Document actual garbage overflow on streets in neighborhoods with highest disposal complaints to verify 311 reports
Report on whether community board's repeated budget requests for facility maintenance equipment would address underlying waste infrastructure needs
